problem: The sentence 'The series arrangement gives more work than one vane because the jet is used again and again' is misleading. In a series of vanes the same water is not reused by successive vanes; each vane is struck by fresh water from the jet. The series gives more work because the full jet mass flow ρaV strikes the vanes, whereas a single vane is struck only by ρa(V − u). A student could wrongly conclude that one parcel of water hits several vanes in turn.
fix: Replace with: 'The series arrangement gives more work than one vane because the full jet mass flow ρaV is deflected, while a single vane is struck only by ρa(V − u).'

problem: The efficiency of a single vane is defined as η = P/(½ρaV³), using the kinetic energy of the whole jet. Only the part ρa(V − u) actually strikes the single vane, so this denominator is not the energy supplied to that vane. The definition is a convention, but the text does not say so, and a student may be confused when comparing single-vane and series efficiency.
fix: State the convention explicitly: 'For a single vane this η uses the whole jet's kinetic energy ½ρaV³ as the input; it is a convention, not the energy of the water that actually strikes the vane.' Alternatively, define single-vane efficiency using the striking mass flow ½ρa(V − u)V² and note that this gives a different peak.

problem: The curve labelled 'flat plate' is the work rate for a single moving flat plate, x(1 − x)². The description does not say 'single moving', so a reader may think it is a series of flat plates, which would be x(1 − x) and would peak at u/V = 0.5, not near 0.33.
fix: Change the description to 'for a single moving flat plate, a single 180° curved vane and a series of vanes' and label the curve accordingly.
